# costfluent_business_metric (Resource)

Manages a Costfluent business metric: a business quantity, such as customers or transactions, whose daily values a cost report divides its cost by. Its values are imported by CSV in the console or through the API, not managed here. Needs a token with `manageBusinessMetrics` and `viewCostReports` on the workspace.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "costfluent_workspace" "production" {
  name     = "Production"
  currency = "USD"
}

# A business metric; its daily values are imported by CSV in the console or through the API
resource "costfluent_business_metric" "customers" {
  workspace_id  = costfluent_workspace.production.id
  name          = "Active customers"
  unit          = "customer"
  label_columns = ["region"]
}

# A report charting cost per customer beside its cost
resource "costfluent_cost_report" "cost_per_customer" {
  workspace_id = costfluent_workspace.production.id
  title        = "Cost per customer"
  settings     = { unit_cost_metric_id = costfluent_business_metric.customers.id }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Metric name.
- `unit` (String) What one unit counts, in the singular, such as customer or transaction.

### Optional

- `label_columns` (List of String) Up to five columns each value is labeled by, such as customer or region. Every stored value is keyed by them, so changing them replaces the metric and its values.
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace ID. When omitted, the provider's default workspace at creation is recorded and kept, so a later change to the provider's default does not move it.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Business metric ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The configuration sets workspace_id: "<workspace ID>:<business metric ID>". Import with that
# workspace, because changing a configured workspace_id recreates the business metric.
terraform import costfluent_business_metric.customers wsp_0000000000000000000001:bmt_0000000000000000000001

# The configuration leaves workspace_id out: the bare business metric ID imports from the
# provider's workspace, which state then keeps.
terraform import costfluent_business_metric.customers bmt_0000000000000000000001
```
